_comment: Registration for the #953 forced-claim prototype, written in the shape
it later is a move, not a rewrite. It is NOT discovered by
scripts/check-negative-controls.py, which scans controls/ - this lives
under docs/research/ because the prototype is a design, not a shipped
Every verdict the checker can emit has at least one case, and the
verdicts that matter have a case on BOTH sides. A checker wedged at
DISAGREE and a working one are indistinguishable without honest-claim;
a counter wedged at UNKNOWN and a working one are indistinguishable

cases.name: inflated-claim
cases.why: Required negative control 1: a claim of 3 tests where the diff contains 1. If this reports VERIFIED the whole design is decoration.

cases.name: honest-claim
cases.why: POSITIVE CONTROL, and load-bearing: without an input that must report VERIFIED, a checker wedged permanently at DISAGREE looks exactly like a working one.

cases.name: passes-on-unfixed
cases.why: Required negative control 2: a named test that PASSES on the pre-fix tree. It discriminates nothing, so tier 2 must refuse it.

cases.name: no-claim
cases.why: #951's state. The checker ran and observed silence - which is why this is ABSENT and not UNKNOWN, and why it is not the same as the step never running.

cases.name: empty-diff
cases.why: #952's amendment: a denominator of ZERO carries the same ambiguity as a missing one and must not read clean.

cases.name: unsignalled-importerror
cases.why: #963's lesson translated to pytest: the pre-fix run exits non-zero via ImportError. A crash is not a match, and scoring it VERIFIED would be a check passing for the wrong reason.

cases.name: absent-claim-tier2-disabled
cases.why: The cost regression, which is silent by construction. The fixture holds 6 tests across 3 files; tier 2 must execute ZERO of them rather than falling back to the whole suite. Without this case, 'disabled on ABSENT' is a sentence in a doc.

cases.name: amendment-reset-unanchored
cases.why: The iterate-until-green hole. With no record the claimant does not author, a discarded-and-refiled claim is indistinguishable from a first filing, so the counter must read UNKNOWN and never 0. A counter that cannot detect its own reset is this design's failure class inside its own remedy.

cases.name: amendment-anchored
cases.why: The counter's POSITIVE CONTROL. Given an anchor carrying 3 distinct claims it must report 2 amendments - a real number. Without this, 'always UNKNOWN' and a working counter are the same instrument.

cases.name: runtime-importerror
cases.why: Codex, HIGH. pytest reports an exception raised INSIDE the test body as FAILED, not ERROR - only a COLLECTION failure is an ERROR. The first cut read 'is FAILED present' and scored a runtime ImportError as a clean assertion match, and unsignalled-importerror hid it by putting the bad import at module scope. This case puts it in the function body.

cases.name: empty-claim-population
cases.why: Codex, HIGH. A claim naming zero tests walked the tier-2 loop zero times and printed 'all 0 failed by assertion' as VERIFIED - scanned 0, clean. #952's amendment violated inside the tool written to enforce it.

cases.name: fails-on-both-trees
cases.why: Codex, MEDIUM. `assert False` fails on the pre-fix tree, so a one-sided check credited it the moment any non-test file changed. Failing before the fix proves nothing unless the test also PASSES on the fix - the same both-sides argument #963 makes for gates, which this design quoted and then applied to one side.

cases.name: empty-anchor
cases.why: Codex, MEDIUM. An anchor that exists and records nothing yielded '0 amendment(s)' and an anchored VERIFIED row, so a record establishing nothing scored like one establishing a clean first filing. A zero-length denominator, one level further in.

cases.name: malformed-claim
cases.why: Codex, MEDIUM. Only json.JSONDecodeError was caught, so valid JSON of the wrong shape raised out of the checker and produced NO BLOCK - indistinguishable from a step that never ran, which is the exact ambiguity this design exists to remove.

cases.name: head-skips
cases.why: Codex pass 2, HIGH. pytest exits 0 for a SKIPPED test as well as a passing one, so a conditional skip on the fixed tree completed a discrimination that never ran. Exit 0 is not 'it passed'; the test must report PASSED. Registered first as UNKNOWN(unsignalled) and corrected: a skip on the FIXED tree reaches the head-run path, so head-unsignalled is the more precise reason. The expectation was wrong, not the behaviour - recorded because adjusting a registration to match observed output is exactly how a control gets laundered into agreement.

cases.name: head-collection-error
cases.why: Codex pass 2, MEDIUM. Every non-pass fixed-tree outcome collapsed into DISAGREE(no-discrimination), so an uninterpretable fixed-tree run was reported as an affirmative contradiction - the same collapse this file refuses for pre-fix crashes, in the other direction.

cases.name: anchor-with-noise
cases.why: Codex pass 2, MEDIUM. The counter counted distinct non-empty LINES, so an unrelated log line became an amendment. Records are parsed and shape-checked now; this anchor carries two log lines and a non-JSON line beside one real claim and must still report 0 amendments.
